methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
1X Technologies, a Pre-Seed stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Bernt Øivind Børnich, presents a valuation challenge within a sector comprising 9 private and 1 public comparable. The company has raised $1.1B to date. The narrow peer set—dominated by companies like Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics—lacks sufficient same-stage or valuation-tier clustering to support a reliable peer-median approach; only 0 same-stage peers and 1 adjacent-stage peer exist within filtering criteria, falling short of the 3+ datapoint minimum for triangulation confidence.

Given these constraints, Stage-Progression analysis provides the only actionable method. Using $2M as a proxy for total raised scaled to early-stage valuation and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Pre-Seed to next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $5M. This represents a conservative calibration against disclosed fund deployment patterns in the robotics sector.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4M–$6M (median $5M). Key uncertainties include the absence of direct stage-peer comparables, which limits confidence in the 2.5x step-up multiplier's applicability to this specific company's risk profile. Additional transparency on investor composition, burn rate, and product-stage milestones would materially refine this estimate.
